In the purge that followed, the Yuwen princes were killed: among them Gan Yun and Xuan of Qiao and Ji, grandsons of the Zhou founder; Shi of Ji, son of Emperor Min; Zhen of Feng and Shi of Song, sons of Emperor Ming; Zan of Han, Zhi of Qin, Yun of Cao, Chong of Dao, Dui of Cai, and Yuan of Jing, sons of Emperor Gaozu; and Yan of Lai and Shu of Ying, sons of Emperor Xuan.
The Duke of Qin is 秦公贄 (Zhi), not a second Zan; the translation duplicated 漢公贊's name. (The literal field repeats the same error.)

In spring, on the renwu day of the first month, Prince Jin'an Bo Gong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Yuan Xian, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Right Vice Director.

In spring, on the renwu day of the first month, Chen Bogong, Prince of Jin'an, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Yuan Xian, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Right Vice Director.
伯恭 is the single given name Bogong of the Chen prince of Jin'an; "Prince Jin'an Bo Gong" splits it as if a surname plus name and garbles the title.

Emperor Xiaowu of Zhou heard of his talent and offered him the posts of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and later Lower Grand Master of Shaobo—Su Wei declined each on grounds of illness;

Emperor Wu of Zhou (Gaozu) heard of his talent and offered him the posts of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and later Lower Grand Master of Shaobo—Su Wei declined each on grounds of illness;
周高祖 is the temple name of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou (Yuwen Yong), not "Emperor Xiaowu".
In the third month, on wuzi, He Ruo Bi was made regional commander of Wuzhou and stationed at Guangling;
In the third month, on wuzi, Heruo Bi was made regional commander of Wuzhou and stationed at Guangling;
賀若弼 has the compound surname Heruo (賀若); "He Ruo Bi" splits it into three syllables as if surname He.
The emperor intended to conquer the south; he asked Gao Jiong for commanders, and Gao recommended He Ruo Bi and Han Qinhu. They were posted on the southern frontier to prepare the campaign in secret.
The emperor intended to conquer the south; he asked Gao Jiong for commanders, and Gao recommended Heruo Bi and Han Qinhu. They were posted on the southern frontier to prepare the campaign in secret.
賀若弼 has the compound surname Heruo (賀若); "He Ruo Bi" mis-splits it.
Wei Chong was a son of Wei Yun.
Wei Chong was a son of Wei Xiong.
The Chinese has a lost character (□); Wei Chong's father was Wei Xiong (韋夐). The translation's "Wei Yun" is unsupported by the text.
The Tuyuhun raided Liangzhou; the emperor sent campaign commander Yuan Xie, Prince of Le'an, with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry against them.
The Tuyuhun raided Liangzhou; the emperor sent campaign commander Yuan Xie, Duke of Le'an, with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry against them.
樂安公 is a ducal title (Duke of Le'an), not Prince.
Northern Zhou law, modeled on Qi statutes, was cumbersome; the emperor ordered Gao Jiong, Zheng Yi, Yang Su, Pei Zheng of the Directorate of Astronomy, and others to revise it.
Northern Zhou law, modeled on Qi statutes, was cumbersome; the emperor ordered Gao Jiong, Zheng Yi, Yang Su, Pei Zheng the Director of the Watches, and others to revise it.
率更令 is Director of the Watches (an office of the crown prince's household), not the Directorate of Astronomy.
Grand Commander Cui Changren, a brother-in-law of the empress, had broken the law and was liable to execution; because of the empress, the emperor wanted to spare him.
Grand Commander Cui Changren, a cousin of the empress, had broken the law and was liable to execution; because of the empress, the emperor wanted to spare him.
中外兄弟 means a cousin (child of a paternal aunt or maternal uncle), not a brother-in-law.
Once enthroned he located his mother's nephew Lü Yongji, posthumously honored his grandfather Shuang Zhou as Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi, and let Yongji inherit the title.
Once enthroned he located his mother's nephew Lü Yongji, posthumously honored his maternal grandfather Lü Shuangzhou as Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi Commandery, and let Yongji inherit the title.
外祖雙周 is the emperor's maternal grandfather, surnamed Lü with given name Shuangzhou; "Shuang Zhou" reads as a different surname, and 齊郡公 is Duke of Qi Commandery.
Daogui was made a third-rank Master of Ceremonies and sent out as governor of Jinan;
Daogui was made Superior Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies and sent out as governor of Jinan;
上儀同三司 is the prestige rank Superior Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, not a "third-rank Master of Ceremonies".
Meanwhile Fan Shulue of Chenliu, another Xiang governor noted for exceptional governance, received an imperial commendation circulated empire-wide and was summoned to head the Ministry of Revenue.
Meanwhile Fan Shulue of Chenliu, another Xiang governor noted for exceptional governance, received an imperial commendation circulated empire-wide and was summoned to be Minister of Agriculture.
司農 is the Minister of Agriculture (Court of the National Granaries), not the Ministry of Revenue.
In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Sui dispatched Master of Diplomatic Reception Zheng Can on a friendly embassy.
In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Sui dispatched Concurrent Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Zheng Zong on a friendly embassy.
鄭摠 is Zheng Zong (摠 = 總), not "Zheng Can"; 兼散騎侍郎 is Concurrent Gentleman Cavalier Attendant, not Master of Diplomatic Reception.
The tribes agreed: "Of the late qaghan's four sons, Shetu is the finest."
The tribes agreed: "Of the sons of the four qaghans, Shetu is the finest."
四可汗子 means the sons of the four (successive) qaghans; Shetu was not a son of the late Tabo Qaghan, so "the late qaghan's four sons" misstates his lineage.
Prince Shixing Shulang, the crown prince's younger brother, had a different mother, Lady Peng.
Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, the crown prince's next younger brother, had a different mother, the Honored Lady Peng.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang". 始興王 is the Prince of Shixing.
As governor of Jiang he was harsh, cunning, and ruthless.
As governor of Jiang, Shuling was harsh, cunning, and ruthless.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
Shulang hated him and secretly hunted for faults with which to prosecute him.
Shuling hated him and secretly hunted for faults with which to prosecute him.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
When Shulang became governor of Yang, he meddled in capital administration; officials who pleased him were recommended for promotion;
When Shuling became governor of Yang, he meddled in capital administration; officials who pleased him were recommended for promotion;
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
Shulang loved looting ancient tombs; Bogu loved hawking; they often roamed the countryside together, grew intimate, and secretly plotted treason.
Shuling loved looting ancient tombs; Bogu loved shooting pheasants; they often roamed the countryside together, grew intimate, and secretly plotted treason.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang". 射雉 is shooting pheasants, not hawking.
As Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bogu reported every court secret to Shulang.
As Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bogu reported every court secret to Shuling.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
In spring, on jiyou of the first month, the emperor fell ill; the crown prince, Prince Shixing Shulang, and Prince of Changsha Shujian attended him at his bedside.
In spring, on jiyou of the first month, the emperor fell ill; the crown prince, Prince of Shixing Shuling, and Prince of Changsha Shujian attended him at his bedside.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang". 始興王 is the Prince of Shixing.
Shulang harbored treacherous designs and told the pharmacy clerk: "The medicine knife is very dull—you had better sharpen it!"
Shuling harbored treacherous designs and told the pharmacy clerk: "The medicine knife is very dull—you had better sharpen it!"
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
In the confusion Shulang ordered his attendants outside to fetch swords.
In the confusion Shuling ordered his attendants outside to fetch swords.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
The attendants misunderstood and brought the ceremonial wooden sword from his court robes; Shulang flew into a rage.
The attendants misunderstood and brought the ceremonial wooden sword from his court robes; Shuling flew into a rage.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
Prince Shujian stood nearby, heard the order, sensed treachery, and watched Shulang closely.
Prince Shujian stood nearby, heard the order, sensed treachery, and watched Shuling closely.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
Shulang snatched the pharmacy knife and slashed at the crown prince's neck; the prince collapsed in a heap;
Shuling snatched the pharmacy knife and slashed at the crown prince's neck; the prince collapsed in a heap;
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
Wet nurse Lady Wu seized Shulang's arm from behind, and the crown prince struggled to his feet;
Wet nurse Lady Wu seized Shuling's arm from behind, and the crown prince struggled to his feet;
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling (romanized Shuling), not "Shulang".
Shulang grabbed the prince's robe, but the prince wrenched free.
Shuling grabbed the prince's robe, but the prince wrenched free.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Shujian grappled with Shulang, tore away the knife, dragged him to a pillar, and bound him with his own robe sleeves.
Shujian grappled with Shuling, tore away the knife, dragged him to a pillar, and bound him with his own robe sleeves.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".

Shulang was powerfully built; he tore free, bolted out the Cloud Dragon Gate, raced to his Eastern Palace, blocked the Qingxi road, freed eastern-city prisoners for his army, and scattered gold and silk as bounty;

Shuling was powerfully built; he tore free, bolted out the Cloud Dragon Gate, raced to his Eastern Palace, blocked the Qingxi road, freed eastern-city prisoners for his army, and scattered gold and silk as bounty;
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
With roughly a thousand men Shulang prepared to hold the capital by force.
With roughly a thousand men Shuling prepared to hold the capital by force.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
In panic Shulang sent his recorder Wei Liang with his ceremonial musicians to Mohe, promising: "If I prevail, you shall be chief minister of the realm."
In panic Shuling sent his recorder Wei Liang with his ceremonial musicians to Mohe, promising: "If I prevail, you shall be chief minister of the realm."
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Shulang sent his confidants Dai Wen and Tan Qi; Mohe arrested them, sent them to the court for execution, and paraded their heads through the eastern city.
Shuling sent his confidants Dai Wen and Tan Qi; Mohe arrested them, sent them to the court for execution, and paraded their heads through the eastern city.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang". The text's 步陵 is a corruption of 叔陵.
Seeing defeat inevitable, Shulang drowned his consort Lady Zhang and seven favorite concubines in a well, led several hundred men across the small ferry toward Xinlin, intending to sail to Sui.
Seeing defeat inevitable, Shuling drowned his consort Lady Zhang and seven favorite concubines in a well, led several hundred men across the small ferry toward Xinlin, intending to sail to Sui.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Bogu tried to slip into an alley when troops appeared; Shulang chased him with drawn sword; Bogu doubled back, and many of Shulang's men threw down their armor and scattered.
Bogu tried to slip into an alley when troops appeared; Shuling chased him with drawn sword; Bogu doubled back, and many of Shuling's men threw down their armor and scattered.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Mohe's groom Chen Zhishen ran Shulang through; he dropped dead; Chen Zhonghua took his head; Bogu died in the melee; from yin through si order was restored.
Mohe's mounted retainer Chen Zhishen met Shuling and stabbed him; he fell, and Chen Zhonghua cut off his head; Bogu died in the melee; from the yin hour to the si hour order was restored.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang". 僵仆 means he fell, after which Chen Zhonghua beheaded him; he did not "drop dead" from the stab.
Shulang's sons were all put to death; Bogu's sons were spared as commoners.
Shuling's sons were all put to death; Bogu's sons were spared as commoners.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Peng Hao was Shuling's maternal uncle.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang". 舅 here is the maternal uncle (brother of his mother, the Honored Lady Peng).
Zheng Xin and Wei Liang had been Shulang's favorites and habitual advisers.
Zheng Xin and Wei Liang had been Shuling's favorites and habitual advisers.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Xiao Mohe became General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of South Xuzhou, enfeoffed Duke Pacifying the Distance, and was given the entire hoard—worth millions—from Shulang's estate.
Xiao Mohe became General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of South Xuzhou, enfeoffed Duke Pacifying the Distance, and was given the entire hoard—worth millions—from Shuling's estate.
The Chen prince 叔陵 is Chen Shuling, not "Shulang".
Sui's Yuan Jingshan marched out from Hankou and sent Senior General Deng Xiaoru with four thousand men against Zengshan.
Sui's Yuan Jingshan marched out from Hankou and sent Deng Xiaoru, Supreme Commander Unequalled in Honor, with four thousand men against Zengshan.
上開府儀同三司 is the prestige rank Supreme Commander Unequalled in Honor (Shang Kaifu Yitong Sansi), not "Senior General".
On wuchen Chen sent envoys to sue for peace with Sui and restore the Hu estates.
On wuchen Chen sent envoys to sue for peace with Sui and returned Hushu to it.
胡墅 is the fortified place Hushu (opposite Jiankang), which Chen handed back to Sui; it is not "the Hu estates".
In summer, on gengyin of the fourth month, Sui general Han Shoushou routed the Turks at Mount Jitou and pillar Li Chong defeated them at Mount Hebei.
In summer, on gengyin of the fourth month, Sui grand general Han Sengshou routed the Turks at Mount Jitou and Pillar of State Li Chong defeated them at Mount Hebei.
韓僧壽 is Han Sengshou (僧 seng), not "Han Shoushou".
On bingshen Prince Yongkang Yin was made crown prince.
On bingshen the emperor's son Yin, Duke of Yongkang, was made crown prince.
永康公 is Duke of Yongkang, not a Prince.
They raided Lan again; Liang commander He Luzi'gan beat them at Keluoqi.
They raided Lan again; Liang commander Helou Zigan beat them at Keluoqi.
賀婁子干 is Helou Zigan (double surname 賀婁, given name 子干), not "He Luzi'gan".
Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yu Kai, famed for ingenuity, was made deputy overseer of construction.
Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yuwen Kai, famed for ingenuity, was made deputy overseer of construction.
宇文愷 is Yuwen Kai (double surname 宇文), not "Yu Kai".
Yu Kai was the younger brother of Xin.
Yuwen Kai was the younger brother of Yuwen Xin.
愷 and 忻 are Yuwen Kai and his elder brother Yuwen Xin (宇文忻), not "Yu Kai".
That year he took a daughter of the Liang ruler as consort of the Prince of Jin and proposed that his son Yang marry Princess Lanling.
That year he took a daughter of the Liang ruler as consort of the Prince of Jin and proposed that the Liang ruler's son Xiao Yang marry Princess Lanling.
其子瑒 is the Liang ruler's son Xiao Yang (蕭瑒), not the Sui emperor's son; "his son Yang" misattributes him.
On renyin Sui proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.
On renyin Chen proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.
The renyin amnesty and change of era (to Zhide) are Chen acts recorded in the Chen annal frame; Sui kept the Kaihuang era, so "Sui proclaimed" is wrong.
Jiang Zong, Director of the Department of Ritual, was made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
Jiang Zong, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Personnel.
祠部尚書 is Minister of Rites and 吏部尚書 is Minister of Personnel; neither is the Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On guiyou Chen sent He Che, Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, and others on a diplomatic mission to Sui.
On guiyou Chen sent He Che, Concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and others on a diplomatic mission to Sui.
兼散騎常侍 is Concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, not a Secretariat post.
They raided Zuo Prefecture next and were beaten back by local troops.
They raided Kuozhou next and were beaten back by its prefectural troops.
廓州 is Kuozhou, not "Zuo Prefecture".
On xinmao the Sui emperor sent Concurrent Regular Attendants Xue Shu and Wang Shao on a diplomatic mission.
On xinmao the Sui emperor sent Concurrent Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary Xue Shu and Wang Shao on a diplomatic mission.
兼散騎常侍 is Concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, not a "Regular Attendant".
Changsun Sheng, serving then as a deputy in Rongding's command, sent word to Apo: "Each time Shetu takes the field, he wins a sweeping victory.
Zhangsun Sheng, serving then as a deputy in Rongding's command, sent word to Apo: "Each time Shetu takes the field, he wins a sweeping victory.
長孫晟 is romanized Zhangsun Sheng (長 read zhang in this double surname), as elsewhere in the chapter.
The Greedy Khan Tanhan had been friendly with Apo; Shabolü seized his people and removed him, and Tanhan fled to Tardu.
Tanhan Qaghan had been friendly with Apo; Shabolü seized his people and removed him, and Tanhan fled to Tardu.
貪汗可汗 is the title Tanhan Qaghan; "the Greedy Khan" is a calque of the transcription, not a name.
Shabolü's cousin Di Qincha led a separate tribe, quarreled with him, and took his men over to Apo.
Shabolü's younger cousin Diqincha led a separate tribe, quarreled with him, and took his men over to Apo.
地勤察 is a single transcribed Turkic name, Diqincha, not a surname Di plus given name; 從弟 is a younger paternal cousin.
Before a court feast the princess told Min: "I gave my brother the empire—there is only you for a son-in-law; I mean to win you the rank of pillar of state;
Before a court feast the princess told Min: "I gave the empire to His Majesty, and you are my only son-in-law; I mean to win you the rank of pillar of state;
至尊 is His Majesty, the Sui emperor (the princess's father), not her brother; 唯一婿 means Min is her only son-in-law.
In the eleventh month he sent Regular Attendant Zhou Fen and Direct Regular Attendant Yuan Yan on a diplomatic mission to Sui.
In the eleventh month he sent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhou Fen and Attendant-in-Ordinary in Regular Service Yuan Yan on a diplomatic mission to Sui.
散騎常侍 is Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and 通直散騎常侍 Attendant-in-Ordinary in Regular Service; "Regular/Direct Regular Attendant" garbles the titles.
In the twelfth month, on yimao, Sui sent Concurrent Regular Attendant Cao Lingze and Direct Regular Attendant Wei Dan on a diplomatic mission.
In the twelfth month, on yimao, Sui sent Concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Cao Lingze and Attendant-in-Ordinary in Regular Service Wei Dan on a diplomatic mission.
兼散騎常侍 is Concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and 通直散騎常侍 Attendant-in-Ordinary in Regular Service, not "Regular/Direct Regular Attendant".

The emperor wished to name Rongding one of the Three Excellencies; he refused, saying: "Wei Qing, Huo Qubing, Liang Ji, and Deng Yu—had any of them lowered himself a little, his house would not have been destroyed."

The emperor wished to name Rongding one of the Three Excellencies; he refused, saying: "The Wei, Huo, Liang, and Deng consort clans—had they lowered themselves a little, their houses would not have been destroyed."
衛、霍、梁、鄧 names the Han consort clans destroyed for arrogance (Wei, Huo, Liang, Deng), not specifically Huo Qubing or Deng Yu, whose houses were not destroyed.
